attempts.raw: {"version":"2b1","blocks":[{"type":"text","text":"The dot product of two vectors \\(\\mathbf{a}\\) and \\(\\mathbf{b}\\) is a scalar defined as \\(\\mathbf{a} \\cdot \\mathbf{b} = |\\mathbf{a}| |\\mathbf{b}| \\cos \\theta\\), where \\(\\theta\\) is the angle between them. Geometrically, it represents how much one vector extends in the direction of the other."},{"type":"text","text":"If the vectors are orthogonal (at 90°), their dot product is zero because \\(\\cos 90^\\circ = 0\\). This means neither vector projects onto the other."},{"type":"text","text":"If the dot product is positive, the projection of one vector onto the other points in the same direction. If negative, the projection points opposite, indicating an angle greater than 90° between them."},{"type":"ui","source":"{\"root\":\"diagram_stack\",\"elements\":{\"diagram_stack\":{\"type\":\"Stack\",\"props\":{},\"children\":[\"vectorA\",\"vectorB\",\"projection\",\"explanation\"]},\"vectorA\":{\"type\":\"Graphic\",\"props\":{\"label\":\"Vector A\",\"items\":[{\"kind\":\"path\",\"d\":\"M50 100 L150 50\"}]}},\"vectorB\":{\"type\":\"Graphic\",\"props\":{\"label\":\"Vector B\",\"items\":[{\"kind\":\"path\",\"d\":\"M50 100 L130 120\"}]}},\"projection\":{\"type\":\"Graphic\",\"props\":{\"label\":\"Projection of B on A\",\"items\":[{\"kind\":\"path\",\"d\":\"M130 120 L130 100 L50 100\"},{\"kind\":\"path\",\"d\":\"M50 100 L130 100\"}]}},\"explanation\":{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Vector A starts at (50,100) and ends at (150,50). Vector B starts at (50,100) and ends at (130,120). The projection of B onto A is the shadow of B along A's direction. The dot product equals the length of A times the length of this projection. Zero dot product means vectors are orthogonal; negative means projection points opposite to A.\"}}}","state":[]}]}
